paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's promises come with a relationship attached. The LORD tells Solomon He has heard his prayer and chosen this temple, and that His eyes and His heart will be there for all time (2 Chronicles 7:12, 16). That's real, warm, solid love. But He also says it's a walk, and Solomon is asked to walk before Him as his father David walked (2 Chronicles 7:17).

Now look at what the LORD says about hard days. If the rain stops, if locusts come, if a plague hits, the answer isn't to panic. He says, "if My people who are called by My name humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land" (2 Chronicles 7:14). Hard days are not the end of the line, baker. The door back to Him is always open, and I know a little something about being found after a long time in the dark.

The warning is just as clear, and I think it's a heavy one. If they forsake Him and serve other gods, the LORD says He will uproot them from the land, and even the temple will become a heap of rubble (2 Chronicles 7:19 to 22). The reason given is simple: they forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers. So the lesson for you today is to stay close, keep your heart turned toward Him, and when you drift, turn around quick. He's listening, and He's been listening this whole time. The story isn't over, friend, so keep your oven warm.
